production_topology: VNEXT_B is the production transport. Since v0.0.104 the extension runs the ESP32 with -icount in lockstep with the Core (setting lasecsimul.mcu.esp32Timing: realtime = default, exact). MTTCG (tcg,thread=multi) and SINGLE_REALTIME were retired on 2026-10-30: the ESP32 adapter always launches QEMU with -icount, and LASECSIMUL_ESP32_EXECUTION_MODE has no effect. The LEGACY transport is not validated by this promotion.
promotion_history_E146: E146 (EVIDENCE.md, 2026-09-09): promoted the E141-production-clean candidate (475C0FC9...) to canonical, limited to a certified N<=8 VNEXT_B+MTTCG Release release. Preflight confirmed the candidate SHA, zero running QEMU, H143 (McuComponent::pollAndDispatchPendingEvents()) still wired to decidePostAckRearm(), HARNESS_BUILD_CONFIG=Release, LASECSIMUL_REQUIRE_RELEASE=1. Along the way, found and fixed a real, reproducible STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN crash in VnextBProductionScaleTest.cpp's negative N=9 capacity-rejection path (a rejected session's Scheduler/attachment was left torn down only at final teardown instead of immediately, corrupting shared state under concurrent real-QEMU sessions) -- fixed by calling stopSimulation() immediately on rejection, verified crash-free across 8+ direct runs (parallel and sequential) after the fix. Also fixed run_production_mwdt.ps1's own external timeout budget (a rejection scenario's extra concurrent-startup contention under processor-affinity restriction genuinely takes longer, up to ~131s observed, not a hang) and added an explicit CAPACITY_REJECTED_AS_DESIGNED classification so a correctly-refused over-capacity request is no longer misreported as a generic runner failure. Pre-promotion gates: capacity guard pure+concurrency tests 64/64, vnext_b_attachment_test PASS, mcu_component_live_poll_thread_test PASS, session_restart_stress_test 15/15, 5 QEMU-side unit tests PASS (unaffected, same QEMU binary), full VNEXT_B+MTTCG Release regression 14/14, B11 N=8 PASS (8/8, clean), negative N=9 CAPACITY_REJECTED_AS_DESIGNED. RESET_WAIT/E131 deliberately NOT used as a promotion gate this episode -- E131_LEGACY_DIAGNOSTIC_ORACLE_RETIRED_AFTER_PRODUCTION_TRACE_REMOVAL (its own oracle depends on 4 diagnostic tracers E141 correctly removed from production; this is a harness/oracle incompatibility, not a functional regression). N=9 through N=16 deliberately not attempted/certified this episode -- see certified_release_session_limit_note.
provenance: E118-AUDIT-2 (2026-09-05): ROOT-CAUSE FIX for the VNEXT_B+MTTCG watchdog-reset storm found auditing E118-AUDIT's own promotion gate (2 of 10 attempts, 9 and 15 unexpected SW_CPU_RESET_REGISTER resets respectively). Both flagged attempts showed the identical signature: exactly one 'Blocked re-entrant IO on MemoryRegion: esp32.i2c at addr: 0x4' warning immediately after the app-cpu-startup reset and immediately before the first unexpected reset, then a repeating alternating-CPU reset cycle with incrementing boot_epoch for the rest of the run. Root cause, confirmed by direct source-code proof (softmmu/memory.c:546-575): every device-owned MemoryRegion's dispatch wrapper sets mr->dev->mem_reentrancy_guard.engaged_in_io=true on entry and clears it via a plain post-call statement ONLY on a normal return from the device's .write callback. E118's own fix has vnext_b_gpio_write() respond to VNEXT_WOULD_BLOCK (a real vCPU hitting a momentarily-full VNEXT_B lane) with cpu_stop_current() + cpu_loop_exit_restore() -- a siglongjmp back into cpu_exec() that unconditionally skips every intervening return, that cleanup included. The first time this fired from inside a reentrancy-guarded device's own dispatch (observed: esp32_i2c's A_I2C_CTR register write), engaged_in_io was left stuck true FOR THE REST OF THE PROCESS -- every subsequent access to that device was rejected outright (MEMTX_ACCESS_ERROR), which is what actually drove the guest's own repeated watchdog-triggered reset/recovery cycle, not a transport-timing or host-scheduling-contention issue (E113's H4 hypothesis is not implicated here). Fixed by setting disable_reentrancy_guard=true on every device MemoryRegion reachable through writeReg()'s VNEXT_B/cpu_loop_exit_restore() path: hw/i2c/esp32_i2c.c, hw/char/esp32_uart.c, hw/gpio/esp32_gpio.c, hw/ssi/esp32_spi.c, hw/misc/esp32_ledc.c, hw/misc/esp32_sens.c, hw/misc/esp32_iomux.c -- the same idiom already used by hw/intc/apic.c, hw/scsi/lsi53c895a.c, hw/misc/bcm2835_property.c, hw/ppc/pnv_lpc.c, hw/intc/loongarch_ipi.c. Safe specifically because this retry path never drops the BQL, so the cross-vCPU race this guard exists to catch (a second vCPU dispatching into the same device during a BQL-released window, e.g. the LEGACY arena's arenaTransactionBegin()) cannot occur through VNEXT_B's synchronous, BQL-held call chain. Validated: a bounded 12-attempt real-firmware reproduction with the fix showed 0/12 storms and 0/12 'Blocked re-entrant IO' warnings (vs. the pre-fix combined sample of 2 storms in 16 attempts); the official 10-attempt promotion gate (re-run with the ALSO-fixed runner, see below) passed 10/10 including unexpectedResets=0 on every attempt. Fixing this exposed a separate, narrower, EXPLICITLY NOT YET RESOLVED finding: at an artificially tiny test-only LASECSIMUL_VNEXT_B_LANE_DEPTH=2 (not the production default), a real vCPU's now-unconditionally-persistent WOULD_BLOCK retry can out-compete the UART TX bottom-half's own cross-process credit-available notify for freshly-freed lane credit often enough to starve it for an extended window -- not reproduced at the production gate's actual (larger) default lane depth, and not chased further in this entry; see EVIDENCE.md E118-AUDIT-2 and NEXT_ACTION.md. Separately, this entry fixed an inconsistency in the E118-AUDIT gate runner itself: its pass/fail calculation never included unexpectedResets, so both flagged attempts were incorrectly recorded as "pass": true in phase6_mttcg_results.json -- extracted into a shared, unit-tested Get-Phase6AttemptClassification (vnext_prototype/mttcg_causality/E118-AUDIT/phase6_gate_lib.ps1 + phase6_gate_lib_test.ps1), and the existing evidence was re-classified in place (not re-run) to correct the record. Prior provenance (E118-AUDIT): two further real production gaps found and fixed -- UART's uart_write() silently dropping a byte's Core-facing effect once its 128-entry backlog (tx_effects[]/tx_effect_count) reached capacity while tx_fifo kept draining independently (fixed: block the calling vCPU before fifo8_push(), replay via cpu_loop_exit_restore() once uart_wake_backlog_waiters() frees a slot); esp32_i2c_do_transaction()'s current_cpu==NULL timer continuation advancing lastCMD/arming the next step on an unpublished VNEXT_WOULD_BLOCK (fixed: leave the completion timer unarmed, revert RSTART's own lastCMD++, retry via esp32_i2c_vnext_credit_available()). vnext_ring_classify() (include/softmmu/vnext_b_classify.h) extracted as a pure, unit-tested function for the occupancy<depth/==depth/>depth contract. Prior provenance (E118): VNEXT_B's original INVALID_BOOT root-cause fix -- vnext_b_gpio_write()/vnext_b_i2c_submit()/vnext_publish_request() used to treat an ordinary full ring (occupancy==depth) identically to genuine corruption (occupancy>depth), both hard-fatal; UART's TX bottom-half (current_cpu==NULL) hitting that branch set the fatal flags without stopping anything, and shared-lane-0 I2C submissions then silently failed for the rest of the run. Fixed with an explicit VNEXT_PUBLISHED/VNEXT_WOULD_BLOCK/VNEXT_FATAL contract. Prior provenance (E117): VnextBAttachment::prepare()/activate() two-phase startup, closing a registration-ordering race between QEMU's first guest activity and Core's wait-dispatcher registration. Prior provenance (E116): startup-barrier candidate (autostart=0, vm_start() gated on Core RUNNING). Prior provenance (E114-AUDIT/E114/E113/E111/E109): see this field's own history before E116, unchanged and superseded only in the sense that this is now a different binary built from a superset of that same fix.

On 57573025: hermetic suite 100 of 100, external-QEMU battery one test at a time 18 of 18 PASS (including mcu_firmware_lasecplot on UART0_TX and GPIO1), cache_wait_e2e_real_qemu 100 of 100 (25 rounds of 4 concurrent). 0020 (softmmu/vnext_b.c, softmmu/icount.c): the realtime controller stretches instruction time only while the simulation loses pace, never to recover accrued lag, and only by what vCPUs busy >= 90% of the window can give back (icount_take_cpu_activity); before, a 1 s boot lag drove an event-driven guest to a 54x stretch and the LasecPlot burst lost up to 290 ms of UART output (2 of 5 realtime windows failed; with LASECSIMUL_LOCKSTEP_TRACE 4 of 4). 0021 (hw/misc/esp32_dport.c, hw/xtensa/esp32.c, target/xtensa/helper.c): the cache on/off is a per-core gate applied in xtensa_cpu_tlb_fill (trap moved to 0x10000000) instead of memory_region_set_enabled (~2 ms memory-map rebuild per toggle, 161 toggles by 620 ms of guest time), and the cache sync invalidates translated code only for pages whose bytes changed (it flushed the whole 4 MB window on every enable). promotion_note_v0107: 2026-11-01 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0022. 0022 is the first batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit. PCNT (irq 48), MCPWM0/1 (irq 39/40) and TWAI (irq 45) were unmapped (Guru Meditation on the first access) and now exist; the counting, waveforms and CAN protocol run in the Core's adapter at the pads, and the QEMU models keep the registers, read the vNext-B snapshot (128 bytes: PCNT counts, MCPWM timer status, TWAI SR/TEC/REC) and take the Core's events through C2A; DPORT TWAI_RST resets the TWAI. promotion_note_v0108: 2026-11-02 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0023. 0023 is the second batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit. HSPI/VSPI: command/address/dummy/data phases, bit lengths, CPOL/CPHA modes 0-3, the trans-done interrupt, lldesc DMA (irq 52-54) and the chip's reset values (items 5, 15). With a Core interrupt armed (snapshot byte 100) soft writes hold the guest too. Reset scope as on the chip (item 18): esp_restart() is SW_CPU_RESET (CPUs only; LEDC and PCNT keep running); a digital reset resets everything, the Core's engines too (0x3FF48FFC); DPORT_PERIP_RST_EN resets each peripheral on both edges (perip-rst lines; adapter module at 0x3FF000C4). UART TX is wire-exact: every FIFO/CLKDIV/CONF0 store reaches the Core from the vCPU at its instant (the bottom-half delivery let the guest see the UART idle while the Core was still sending, and esp_restart()/deep sleep cut the end of the output); ST_UTX_OUT, TXFIFO_CNT without the shifter, TX_DONE latched (it was inverted). eFuse READ takes 10 us (was a 100 ms placeholder: 300 ms in the ROM per boot, and after a core reset on the PLL the 325 ms TG0 flash-boot WDT fired in the bootloader). Deep sleep: timer/ext0/ext1 wakeups, DEEPSLEEP_RESET keeping RTC memory, the RTC memory CRC engine (RTC_CNTL 0x100/0x104), the TIMG watchdogs off with the digital domain, RTC FAST data reachable by the APP CPU (IDF reads s_adc_tsen_enabled there from core 1). Light sleep: timer/ext0/GPIO wakeups; CCOUNT, TIMG and FRC hold while the clocks are gated; an APB change no longer recounts the timers. The first legacy writeReg inside qemu_init() no longer aborts on the uninitialized arena lock. Measured on 512C581F: external-QEMU battery 31/31 one at a time, including mcu_spi_modes, mcu_soc_reset (3 boots: CPU reset keeps PCNT 19->106 and the PWM, periph_module_reset and SW_SYS_RST reset them), mcu_deep_sleep (timer 361 ms of RTC incl. boot, ext0, ext1 status GPIO33) and mcu_light_sleep (esp_timer 199 ms for 200 ms; CCOUNT and TIMG count only the awake ms); mcu_twai_bus 13 s (was ~150 s, the eFuse wait); class project II1P06, 8 sessions at once: 8/8 at 0.993-1.014x, every LCD sample right. Not modeled: Core peripheral clock gating in light sleep (6b), RTC IO hold, ULP, touch and UART wakeup.
promotion_note_v0109: 2026-11-02 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0024. 0024 is the third batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit; it ships with mcu_abi 3.5 (get_pin_analog) and the adapter's RtcIo and Soc modules (19 modules). Touch (item 7): the SENS touch FSM (sleep, XPD, measurement window) counts T * I * slope / (2 * (20 pF + C_ext) * dV) with I = 1.72 uA per slope step and dV from TOUCH_CFG; the Core measures C_ext of each pad's net with a staged 1 MOhm / 1 us probe, delivered through the snapshot before the window ends; SENS channels 8/9 swapped as on the chip; the threshold interrupt and the deep-sleep touch wakeup. RTC IO: a pad muxed to the RTC domain loses the digital output and RTC_GPIO OUT/ENABLE drive it, with the RUE/RDE pulls; QEMU forwards RTC_GPIO_OUT/ENABLE and the pad registers to the Core. DAC (item 8): GPIO25/26 at 3.3 * D / 255 through 20 Ohm (an analog pin drive, Norton stamp). The digital reset now runs in the adapter (Soc module at 0x3FF48FFC) and keeps the RTC domain and the pad voltages; the QEMU-side RTC IO resync was removed (17 writeRegs in one replayable store livelocked). UART (item 9): parity, 5-8 data bits, 1/1.5/2 stop bits and RS485_CONF DL0/DL1 (ESP-IDF sends 2 stop bits as STOP_BIT_NUM 1 + DL1_EN), TXD_INV/RXD_INV, the receive errors (PARITY_ERR, FRM_ERR, BRK_DET latched, RXFIFO_OVF; the byte is still stored) through C2A payload byte 2, and the TX break (TXD_BRK, TX_BRK_NUM, TX_BRK_DONE; uart_write_bytes_with_break() waited forever); QEMU paces the frame with the Core's integer formula. Measured on 8864A0CA: external-QEMU battery 34/34 one at a time, including mcu_touch (bare pad 70, 100 pF 11, 470 pF 2; deep-sleep wake cause 5 pad 3), mcu_dac (64/128/192 -> 828/1656/2485 mV; DAC2 200 into 1 kOhm 2537 mV; RTC GPIO drives the pad) and mcu_uart_format (32 bytes 8N1 2790 us, 8E1 3069 us, 8N1.5 2930 us, 5N1 1955 us; parity/frame/break detected; the break call returns in 969 us for 110 bits); class project II1P06, 8 sessions at once: 8/8 at 1.000-1.002x, every LCD line right. promotion_note_v0110: 2026-11-02 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0025. 0025 is the fourth batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit; it ships with the adapter's I2S DAC stream (RtcIo 0xF0-0xF8), I2S ADC sampler (ADC module 0x3C0-0x3D0) and I2C slave engine. I2S (item 11): new I2S0/I2S1 devices (they were unimplemented stubs and i2s_write()/i2s_read() waited forever): TRM reset values; an exact rational entry period from PLL_F160M or the APLL; TX lldesc DMA through the 64-entry FIFO (OUT_DONE, OUT_EOF per OUT_EOF_MODE, OUT_TOTAL_EOF), RX DMA (IN_DONE, IN_SUC_EOF per RXEOF_NUM), the CPU FIFO mode; RX reads the DIN pin level; a slave runs only off the other half through SIG_LOOPBACK. Built-in DAC mode: each sample's upper byte to DAC1 (right)/DAC2 (left) at its instant. Built-in ADC mode: the Core samples the SAR pattern table's pads at the sample instants and QEMU converts them (adc1_get_raw's transfer function). New APB_CTRL device (it was a stub; DATE keeps the ECO3 marker) with the SAR ADC digital controller. The APLL: the analog I2C host register returns the APLL block's registers and a done calibration (use_apll used to hang in rtc_clk_apll_coeff_set). eFuse without an image: the factory fuses of an ESP32-D0WD-V3 (rev1, rev2, D0WD package); it read as revision 0 and ESP-IDF ran its rev-0 workarounds. The ECO3 interrupt-watchdog livelock handler now runs (stage 0 at 20 ms, both CPUs in it): guest_cache_wait_e2e feeds TG1 while it holds CPU1 on purpose. I2C slave (item 12): the Core's engine on SCL/SDA (7-bit address, ACK, RX/TX FIFO bytes after SDA_HOLD, no clock stretching like the original ESP32); QEMU keeps the FIFOs, RXFIFO_FULL/TXFIFO_EMPTY/TRANS_COMPLETE and STATUS SLAVE_RW/SCL_MAIN_STATE_LAST; I2C_CTR resets to 0x3 (slave). Measured on 5B26C905: external-QEMU battery 38/38 one at a time, including mcu_i2s (441-frame TX_DONE every 10000 us at 44.1 kHz, 55125 us at 8 kHz, 10000 us with use_apll; 1 s of i2s_write in 1.000004 s; 1600 RX samples in 100000 us equal to the DIN level), mcu_i2s_dac (828/2485 mV and swapped; a 0/255 square every 19999 us; dacWrite after uninstall 1294 mV), mcu_i2s_adc (I2S code 1879 = adc1_get_raw 1879; a 1 kHz square at 20 kHz: 200 edges 20.00 samples apart, 2000/4000 high, 4000 samples in 200000 us) and mcu_i2c_slave (two ESP32s: 3 writes ACKed, the slave got hi0..hi2, reads ABCD/EFGH/IJKL); class project II1P06, 8 sessions at once: 8/8 at 1.000x with all 23 display lines in the third run; the second had 7/8 at 1.000x and one at 0.981x, the first, right after the battery, 0.951-0.992x. promotion_note_v0111: 2026-11-02 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0026. 0026 is the fifth batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit (item 13); it ships with the adapter's APB_CLK report (Soc module 0x3FF48FF8). The CPU clock: APB_CTRL_SYSCLK_CONF.PRE_DIV_CNT divides XTAL and RC_FAST (setCpuFrequencyMhz(20)/(10) stayed at 40 MHz), and the APLL is a CPU source (CPUPERIOD_SEL 0: APLL/4, 1: APLL/2, APB = CPU/2). QEMU reports APB_CLK to the Core on each change (the adapter starts at 40 MHz, XTAL): LEDC (timers on APB keep counting at the new rate), the PCNT filter, MCPWM capture, the TWAI TQ, the I2C SCL period and the UART bit time follow it; the UART bit is 1e9 / ((APB << 4) / CLKDIV) on both sides from the raw divider (UART 0xF10), so the wire stays exact. The I2C period went to the Core after being stored, so a replayed store never resent it. Measured on 62193BC1: external-QEMU battery one at a time 37/39, then 39/39 with the two below, including mcu_cpu_freq (240/160/80 MHz on the PLL and 40/20/10 MHz on the divided XTAL: getCpuFrequencyMhz and getApbFrequency right, CCOUNT 240/160/80/40/19/10 per us, a re-set-up 1 kHz LEDC at 996-1002 us); esp32_adapter (hermetic) failed until it reported the 80 MHz APB before its LEDC checks; mcu_scheduler_pacing_sync_real_qemu failed once (12.5 s scheduler gap) and passed in two reruns on this binary and once on 5B26C905; class project II1P06, 8 sessions at once: third run 7 at 1.000x and one at 1.025x (catching up), the first two runs (right after other tests) 0.967-1.006x and 0.977-1.030x. Not modeled: REF_TICK other than 1 MHz.
promotion_note_v0112: 2026-11-02 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0027. 0027 is the sixth batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit (item 3b), adding ESP32 RMT RX. QEMU forwards per-channel RX_EN, FILTER_EN, FILTER_THRES, IDLE_THRES and APB tick to the Core; the adapter filters in APB cycles and queues pulse items and the RX end at their deadlines; the Core delivers events to 0x3FF56480 and schedules the RMT hard wakeup at 0x50C. RX_END sets INT_RAW bit 3n+1; ERR sets bit 3n+2 if RX RAM overflows or MEM_OWNER is 0. CONF1 RX_EN is bit 1 and MEM_WR_RST bit 2, as the TRM specifies. The original ESP32 has no RX carrier demodulation or ping-pong; tick rounding omits counter phase. Measured on F59B3C15: external-QEMU battery 40/40 one at a time; mcu_rmt_rx reports 12 events, filters the 1 us pulse at 100 cycles and ends after IDLE_THRES. Three II1P06 class runs, 8 sessions each: all 24 sessions at 1.000x-1.005x with 22-23 correct LCD/PCD lines per session.
promotion_note_v0113: 2026-11-02 (deployed to devices/qemu-esp32/bin, not yet released): 7ead728 + patches 0011-0028. 0028 is the seventh batch of the ESP32 peripheral-fidelity audit (item 6b). On light sleep entry, QEMU publishes the digital clock gate to Soc 0x3FF48FF4 before stalling the guest; bit 1 reports RTC8M retained when RTC_CNTL_CLK_CONF.CK8M_FORCE_PU is set. The timer/external/GPIO wake callback publishes clock restore and retries on lane backpressure before resuming the guest. The adapter freezes APB/REF_TICK LEDC, PCNT filtering/counting, MCPWM, RMT TX/RX, TWAI, UART, I2C and SPI work; shifts their deadlines/epochs on wake; and leaves low-speed LEDC on RTC8M running only when retained. The new mcu_light_sleep_periph test configures high-speed APB and low-speed RTC8M LEDC loopbacks into PCNT, measures a 50 ms timer sleep and verifies PCNT accumulated at most two edges across the wake boundary; it does not directly observe RTC8M output during sleep. Measured: external-QEMU battery 41/41 one at a time (mcu_scheduler_pacing_sync_real_qemu 91 s; mcu_i2c_slave 152 s), including mcu_light_sleep and mcu_light_sleep_periph. Three II1P06 runs with 8 concurrent sessions: A and C all 1.000x; B six 1.000x, one 0.995x and one 1.022x; every session had 22-23 correct LCD/PCD lines.
